brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: piece:0,0,0;half-n and piece:0,0,1;half-n are stacked and joined by snap:0,0,0;half-n.
drawer:0#0,0#cut on storey 1 and drawer:1#0,0#cut on storey 2.

It takes up one cell on the bench, with capped faces, bolted joints and a top cover (cover:0,0,1;half-n;top). Pliers are shown in the upper drawer and gaffer tape on top. No props would fit in the lower drawer, so it is shown empty. The configurator checks fit only, so how much weight it can hold is not verified.

finish.summary: I built a two-storey storage tower with one drawer on each storey. It's two north-half hex bases stacked one on the other and snapped together, with a drawer in the cut face of each. The open faces are closed with solid end caps, the joints are bolted, and there's a cover on top that gives a small flat surface. The parts budget is 23 parts, about 1229 g of filament and 1770 minutes of printing. check_build found no rule issues and the mesh-collision check came back clear. For staging, pliers sit in the upper drawer and a roll of gaffer tape sits on the top cover. Nothing would fit in the lower drawer: three props were refused because they overlapped the drawer or a wall, so it is shown empty.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
